pride_data.title: An inhibitory segment within G-patch activators tunes Prp43-ATPase activity during ribosome assembly
pride_data.projectDescription: Chemical cross-linking coupled to mass spectrometry using the amine-reactive DSS reagent was used to study the interactions between the RNA helicase Prp43 and its interactors, Pxr1 and Tma23, in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Chemical cross-linking was performed following previously described procedures (Leitner et al., Nat. Protoc., 2014). DSS cross-linking was performed at 0.25 mM and 1 mM final concentrations, and samples were digested using endoproteinase Lys-C followed by trypsin. The digested samples were analyzed by data-dependent LC-MS/MS on a Thermo Orbitrap Fusion Lumos system with duplicate injections. Additional experimental details are provided in the accompanying publication.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: MS/MS spectra were searched using xQuest (Walzthoeni et al., Nat. Methods, 2012), version 2.1.5, against a database containing the sequences of the target proteins (including tags), and the contaminant protein, ARNA_ECOLI. Methionine oxidation was specified as a variable modification, while carbamidomethylation of cysteine was set as a fixed modification. Protease specificity was set to cleavage after K and R unless followed by P, with a maximum of two missed cleavages per peptide allowed (excluding the cross-linking site). The precursor mass error was initially set to ±15 ppm, and the precursor mass window was further adjusted to -5 to 0 ppm post-search. Fragment mass error tolerance was set to 0.2 Da for common ions (not containing the crosslinking site) and 0.3 Da for xlink ions (containing the crosslinking site). Primary search results were further filtered with a minimum TIC value of 0.1, a delta score of ≤0.9 and a mions score of ≥3. Using an xQuest score cut-off of 16, the estimated false discovery rate (FDR) was less than 5% for intra-protein links at the level of non-redundant peptide pairs. A reliable estimate of inter-protein FDR was not possible due to the small number of hits. All inter-protein candidate cross-links were therefore additionally manually evaluated. All cross-link identifications are compiled in a spreadsheet in Microsoft Excel format that is included with the submission. The spreadsheet “File_list.xlsx” connects the raw file names with individual samples and cross-linking conditions. Additional experimental details are provided in the accompanying publication.
keywords: Chemical cross-linking; dss; structural proteomics; ribosome assembly
